new_value: LSU's band began in 1893 as an eleven-member cadet band organized by two students, Wylie M. Barrow and Ruffin G. Pleasant, a future governor, when the university stood in downtown Baton Rouge. It was a marching unit by about 1900, appeared at Mardi Gras festivities in New Orleans, and made its first football halftime appearance in 1924. In the 1930s Governor Huey P. Long brought in Castro Carazo, orchestra leader at the Roosevelt Hotel in New Orleans, as bandmaster, grew the band to nearly 250 members, and co-wrote "Touchdown for LSU," still the main song of the pregame show in Tiger Stadium. The band's present hall on Aster Street opened in late 2011.
